title: Push and Pull
subtitle: How things start, stop and roll
subject: Physics

p: Push the door. It swings open.
Push the swing. Off it goes.
A push moves things away from you. Can you push the air with your hand?
pages.cap: Push the cart and away it rolls.
pages.fact: Did you know? Even the wind is a push. Air is pushing on you right now.

p: Pull the rope. Pull your sock on.
A pull moves things closer to you.
Try it. Pull your own ear, very gently. That is a pull.
pages.cap: Pull the rope down and the load goes up.

pages.q: You tug a wagon along behind you. Is that a push or a pull?
pages.why: The wagon comes closer to you, so it is a pull.

p: Tap a ball. It rolls a little.
Kick the ball. It zooms away!
A big push makes a big move. A little push makes a little move.
pages.cap: The harder the push, the farther the ball goes.

p: Every toy, every ball, every door needs a push or a pull to get going. Look around. What pushed that?
A push can start things. A push can stop things too.
Catch a rolling ball. Your hands push it. It stops.
Can you stop a ball with just one finger?
pages.cap: Push down on one end and the other end goes up.

p: You need a toy car and a smooth floor.
steps: Give the car a soft push. Watch where it stops.
Bring it back. Give it a hard push.
Which push sent it farther? Try a medium push too.
pages.cap: Soft push, short trip. Hard push, long trip.
pages.safe: Push cars along the floor, not at people.

p: Drop a ball. It falls down. Never up!
Something is pulling it. You cannot see it.
That pull is called gravity. Gravity pulls everything down to the ground.
pages.cap: Gravity pulls on planets too. It keeps them circling the Sun.
pages.fact: Did you know? Gravity pulls the Moon toward Earth. That is why the Moon stays with us.

p: Jump up as high as you can.
Gravity pulls you right back down. Every single time.
A rocket pushes so hard it beats gravity. Up, up and away!
pages.cap: The rocket pushes hot gas down. The gas pushes the rocket up.

pages.q: An apple drops from a tree. What pulls it down?
pages.why: Gravity pulls everything down toward the ground, apples too.

p: Round things roll. A ball rolls. A wheel rolls.
A box does not roll. It slides and stops.
Look for round things. Which ones can roll?
pages.cap: Wheels are round, so the cart rolls easily.

p: Push a swing. It goes up.
Gravity pulls it back down. Then up the other side.
Back and forth. Back and forth. Slower and slower, until it stops.
pages.cap: A swing is a push, then a pull, then a push again.

pages.h: A seesaw turns a push down into a push up.
p: You push down on your side. The board pushes your friend up. Then your friend pushes down and up you go!
Put a toy boat in the bath. It floats.
The water is pushing it up!
Drop in a stone. Gravity wins. Down it sinks.
pages.cap: Water pushes the boat up. Gravity pulls the stone down.

p: You need a bowl of water and some small things.
steps: Guess first. Will the spoon float or sink?
Drop it in. Were you right?
Try a cork, a coin, a leaf and a crayon.
pages.cap: Some things float. Some things sink.
pages.safe: Do this with a grown-up and keep water away from plugs.

p: A magnet pulls with no hands.
Hold it near a paper clip. Watch the clip jump!
You cannot see the pull. But it is there.
pages.cap: The pull of a magnet reaches out all around it.
pages.fact: Did you know? A fridge magnet is pulling on the fridge door all day and all night.

p: A magnet pulls iron and steel.
It does not pull wood. It does not pull plastic. It does not pull you!
Try the magnet on a spoon, a cup and a coin.
pages.cap: Iron and steel feel the pull. Wood and plastic do not.

pages.q: Which one will a magnet pull?
pages.why: Magnets pull iron and steel. The paper clip is steel.

p: Two magnets can pull together. Snap!
Now turn one magnet around.
They push apart! You can feel it. Try to make them touch.
pages.cap: Same ends push apart. Different ends pull together.

p: Some pushes are too big for you.
Pulleys can let a small pull lift a big load.
Gears turn each other. One push, many turns!
pages.cap: Turn one gear and the others turn too.

p: Bend your arm. Feel the bump? That is a muscle.
Muscles pull on your bones to move you.
Your heart pushes blood, too. Thump, thump!
pages.cap: Muscles pull on bones to make you move.

p: Push the toothbrush. Pull the blanket.
Push the door. Pull the zip.
You push and pull hundreds of times a day. Can you count ten?
pages.cap: Pushes and pulls get you through the whole day.

items: to move something away from you
to move something closer to you
the pull that makes things fall down
to turn over and over as you move
a thing that pulls iron and steel
to stay on top of the water

qs: What is the biggest thing you can push? What is the biggest thing you can pull?
If gravity went away for one minute, what would happen to your toys?
Where would you put a magnet to be useful at home?
